clue.text: In sacred space, a remarkable intuition returned

indicators.note: returned means the letters are sent back the way they came, so read backwards

parts.note: ESP, extrasensory perception, is a remarkable sort of intuition

explanation.surface: Someone senses something uncanny while standing in a church.
explanation.definitionFit: The semicircular recess at the east end of a church is a sacred space, typically holding the altar.

clue.text: One not confirmed in high office, as Orangeman is

definitions.text: One not confirmed in high office
definitions.meaning: a rival claimant to the papacy, elected but never recognised by the Church
a member of the Protestant Orange Order is opposed to the Pope

explanation.walkthrough: The Orange Order is a Protestant fraternity in Northern Ireland, famously hostile to Roman Catholicism.
explanation.definitionFit: A rival pontiff set up against the canonically elected one never had his title confirmed; read as two words it describes an opponent of the papacy.

clue.text: Support including label that may put price up

indicators.note: including means the first word's letters hold the second inside them

parts.note: a shore is a prop or support, as for a wall
a tag is a label

explanation.surface: A display stand carries a price label that pushes prices higher.
explanation.definitionFit: When supply falls short of demand, scarcity drives prices upward, so a lack of goods may raise costs.

clue.text: Aim bullet, so unlikely to miss

parts.note: to point a weapon is to aim it
a blank is a cartridge without a proper bullet, here loosely called one

explanation.surface: A marksman takes aim and fires, confident of a hit.
explanation.definitionFit: Shooting from very close range means a shot is almost certain to hit its target.

clue.text: Arts building has to suffice over a long time

indicators.note: over means the word for suffice is turned backwards

parts.note: do means suffice, as in that will do
an eon is an immensely long period

explanation.surface: An arts centre has to make do for ages.
explanation.walkthrough: The Odeon was a Greek concert hall long before it named a cinema chain; 'has to' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: In ancient Greece a roofed hall for musical performances, the origin of the cinema chain's name.

clue.text: Make unfeeling revolutionary enter centre of government

parts.note: to numb is to make unfeeling

indicators.note: revolutionary signals the letters of the next word are turned round into a new order

explanation.surface: A radical deadens feeling before marching into the seat of power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make unfeeling' looks like an instruction, but it supplies a word; 'revolutionary' is the anagram signal, not a rebel.
explanation.definitionFit: Number 10 Downing Street is the British Prime Minister's residence and office, the hub of UK government.

clue.text: Huge feat of engineering said to be feature of Venice

indicators.note: said means we want what sounds like the phrase, not its spelling

parts.note: a great big span over water could be called a bridge of size

explanation.surface: A tourist guide talks up a marvel of Venetian construction.
explanation.definitionFit: The enclosed limestone footbridge over the Rio di Palazzo is one of the city's famous landmarks.

clue.text: Creative artist's hour at work

indicators.note: at work means the letters are busy being rearranged

explanation.surface: An artist spends an hour working.
explanation.definitionFit: A writer is a creator of literary art, the originator of a book or poem.

clue.text: Economist sent up to hunt round US city

indicators.note: in a down clue sent up means the whole thing is read from bottom to top
round means the letters of the hunting word go around the city

parts.note: to seek is to hunt for
NY is short for New York

explanation.surface: An economist is mocked for scouring an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'sent up' turns the whole container upside down, not just the hunting word.
explanation.definitionFit: John Maynard Keynes was the influential British economist behind Keynesian theory.

clue.text: Spot of disturbance that may need someone to shoot?

definitions.text: Spot of disturbance that may need someone to shoot?

parts.words: Spot of disturbance that may need someone to shoot?
parts.note: a bit of bother calls for a fixer of problems, whose job title ends in shooter

explanation.surface: Unrest that seems to call for a gunman.
explanation.walkthrough: The shooter is a troubleshooter, someone who solves problems, not a gunman.
explanation.definitionFit: Disturbance and bother are synonyms, and a spot of it is what a troubleshooter is hired to fix.

clue.text: Notice here what murderer intends at AGM?

definitions.text: Notice here what murderer intends at AGM?

parts.words: Notice here what murderer intends at AGM?
parts.note: a killer at a company meeting might plan to put a shot into the directors

explanation.surface: A killer plots mayhem at a company's annual general meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: An AGM is a company's annual general meeting, attended by its board of directors.
explanation.definitionFit: A noticeboard is where notices are pinned up for people to read.

clue.text: As a rule, I stayed in, in soppy fashion

indicators.note: stayed in means the letter sits inside the other word

parts.note: mostly means generally, as a rule

explanation.surface: Someone who habitually stays home is rather wet.
explanation.definitionFit: Soppy here means soaked, so behaving in a damp, wet way.

clue.text: Irritation in particular with university blade

parts.note: pet as an adjective means special or particular, as in a pet project
a lance is a weapon, here a blade, also the verb for cutting with a scalpel

explanation.surface: Annoyance at a university's choice of weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: Peevish irritation and sulky ill temper are what petulance means.

clue.text: Go, could one say, for one on hand?

indicators.note: the letter O could be spoken as love, the tennis word for nil

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A question about the board game Go played with one hand.
explanation.walkthrough: O is called love in tennis scoring, so GO becomes G plus LOVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Mittens and gauntlets are worn on the hand, as any covering for fingers is.

clue.text: Thoughts of Empress of Blandings coloured by this?

parts.note: the prize pig of Blandings Castle in P G Wodehouse's stories
mentation means thinking or mental activity

explanation.surface: A question of what colours a prize sow's musings.
explanation.walkthrough: In P G Wodehouse's Blandings novels the Empress is Lord Emsworth's prize sow.
explanation.definitionFit: Natural colouring of skin or tissue comes from pigments, so things are coloured by it.

clue.text: Daily part he played, holding stage

indicators.note: holding means the anagrammed letters wrap round the stage word
played means the letters are rearranged as if performed differently

parts.note: a leg is a stage of a journey or race

explanation.surface: An actor's role includes a scene on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Daily' looks like an adverb; it is the definition, a newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: The Daily Telegraph is a British national newspaper, often called just the Telegraph.

clue.text: Fowler gave page a folio

annotationWithheld.why: Fowler gave page a folio: Fowler defines Papageno, but no reading of 'gave page a folio' builds the letters (PA+PAGE+NO would need words for father and number); clue appears OCR-garbled and the scan is blank

clue.text: Game on! — that's unknown for one laureate

indicators.note: for here means one letter stands in place of another

parts.note: tennis is a game
I is the Roman numeral one
Y is an algebraic unknown, like x

explanation.surface: Excitement as a match begins.
explanation.walkthrough: TENNIS ON with Y put in place of I gives the poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred, Lord Tennyson was Britain's Poet Laureate for over forty years.

clue.text: Swearing, get a move to Accounts

indicators.note: to means the rearranged letters are added after the accounts word

parts.note: billings are invoices or accounts

indicators.note: move means the letters shift into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone curses and is told to go and work in Accounts.
explanation.definitionFit: Coarse abusive language, named after the London fish market whose porters were famous for it.

clue.text: Part of head given a good squeeze is and the painful

annotationWithheld.why: Part of head given a good squeeze is and the painful: A(CHIN)G gives the letters, but 'is and the' is OCR garbage not in any sound clue, and the blank scan cannot show the printed text
annotationWithheld.clue: Part of head given a good squeeze is and the painful

clue.text: Announcement of maths discovery that went with a splash?

definitions.text: Announcement of maths discovery that went with a splash?

parts.words: Announcement of maths discovery that went with a splash?
parts.note: the cry attributed to Archimedes on jumping from his bath after grasping displacement

explanation.surface: A mathematician celebrates a breakthrough made in the bath.
explanation.walkthrough: Archimedes supposedly ran from the bath shouting the word after realising how displaced water measures volume.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek exclamation means I have found it, the cry of sudden discovery.

clue.text: Comfort food, tiny amount

definitions.meaning: the soft inside of a loaf, bread being the classic comforting food
a very small bit, as in not a scrap of evidence

explanation.definitionFit: A morsel of bread is both a bit of food and, figuratively, the smallest amount, as in a morsel of comfort.

clue.text: Alcohol round start of speech, then water, for silk

indicators.note: round means the drink's letters surround the next letter

parts.note: grog is rum and water, or alcohol generally

indicators.note: start of picks the first letter of the word speech

parts.note: rain is water falling from the sky

explanation.surface: A drink, a speech and a splash of water before choosing silk.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy ribbed fabric, typically silk, used for ribbons and trimmings.

clue.text: Somewhat flat column erected with Call 0870 unusual base

annotationWithheld.why: Somewhat flat column erected with Call 0870 unusual base: hidden reversal in 'flat column' gives the letters, but 'with Call 0870' is foreign OCR text (an advertisement number) and the blank scan cannot show the printed clue
annotationWithheld.clue: Somewhat flat column erected with Call 0870 unusual base

clue.text: General to veto a Japanese occupation

parts.note: Ike was the nickname of General Dwight Eisenhower
to ban is to veto

explanation.surface: An American general blocks a Japanese takeover.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a military occupation; the occupation is a pastime.
explanation.definitionFit: The traditional Japanese art of flower arranging is a pursuit or pastime.

clue.text: Son tucks into vegetables, just a little of each

indicators.note: tucks into means the letter goes inside the vegetables word

parts.note: taters is a colloquial word for potatoes

explanation.surface: A boy eats his vegetables but only nibbles each one.
explanation.definitionFit: Small sample portions offer a mouthful of each dish, as in a tasting menu.

clue.text: Youngster rebuked about pound to be added to large sum

indicators.note: to be added to means the inner build follows the sum

parts.note: a grand is a thousand pounds

indicators.note: about means the scolding word goes around the pound sign

parts.note: chid is an old past tense of chide, to rebuke
L stands for pound, from the Latin libra

explanation.surface: A child is told off over money added to a big total.
explanation.definitionFit: A child's child is a young member of the family, a youngster to grandparents.

clue.text: Knock out a new riddle

parts.note: KO is the abbreviation for a knockout

explanation.surface: A puzzle so hard it floors you.
explanation.definitionFit: A paradoxical Zen puzzle used to provoke enlightenment is a kind of riddle.
